objections.claim: The spec's smoke-test preamble states "All eight FAFF-825 steps, unchanged in definition," but the step-6 procedure text adds a requirement the FAFF-825 original does not carry: "and that the nearest preceding heading is the one the map names." A builder following the DONE item "keep the step definitions" versus the inline procedure text receives two different step-6 definitions, and the map's recorded smoke-test run will claim fidelity to a procedure it has silently extended.
objections.evidence: Spec section 8, "Integration smoke test" preamble ("All eight FAFF-825 steps, unchanged in definition") versus step 6's added heading-verification clause; compare the FAFF-825 map's own step-6 row, which checks verbatim quotation only.
objections.predicted_consequence: The revised map's smoke-test record asserts it re-ran the FAFF-825 procedure unchanged while actually running a stricter step 6 — or a builder drops the heading check to honour "unchanged," and a mis-attributed quote survives. Either way the audit trail misstates what was checked.

objections.claim: Today, `test/shadow-fidelity.test.mjs`'s "the committed FAFF-826 report reproduces from a clean context" case is the sole automated check that exercises `readMapDecisionKernelCommands` against the **live** map: if a future edit to `STATE-AUTHORITY-MAP-v5.md` corrupts the classification table's parseability (a malformed row, a stray cell that shifts the bucket column, a row the regex silently stops matching), the banked reproduction breaks and CI fails. The spec repoints that case at a committed fixture root, after which **no committed test parses the live map at all**. `resolveMapCommands` is explicitly fail-open by design ("tolerating an absent map … by returning the empty set and a reason, so `run` never hard-crashes"), so a post-merge edit that degrades the live map's parseability silently changes the parsed decision-kernel set — and therefore the shadow study's in-scope and set-aside derivation on every subsequent `faff shadow-fidelity run` — with no CI signal. The spec's own anti-drift controls (step 6a's column-aware equality check, the RowChange shape constraint) are build-time procedures in this ticket, not committed enforcement; they die with the build. The follow-up issue (manifest digest pinning in `cmdReproduceVerb`) is a bin/lib change that cannot land under this ticket's constraint, so the window has no replacement control, only a named finding.
objections.evidence: Spec §"The shadow-fidelity coupling" (chosen option: "Point the CI reproduce case at a committed fixture root"); §4 step 6c.iii edits only that one case; §2 out-of-scope excludes all `bin/lib` changes including "making `shadow-fidelity reproduce` read the map revision a result was produced under"; `shadow-fidelity.js :: resolveMapCommands` ("tolerating an absent map … returning the empty set"); §4 step 6a's check exists only in the PROCEDURE, not in any deliverable file.
objections.predicted_consequence: After merge, a map edit that breaks or shifts the classification table's regex match silently alters `faff shadow-fidelity run`'s scope derivation (kernels silently set aside or included in the FAFF-826/FAFF-974 fidelity measurement) with CI green; the drift is discovered only when a human re-runs reproduce against the live root and gets exit 1, which nothing schedules.

objections.claim: The rewritten smoke-test procedure requires that for each quoted fragment "the nearest preceding heading is the one the map names" — but the map (per the prior revision's convention, which this spec keeps) names files and line numbers for quotes, not source headings. For any quote whose source heading the map does not name, the check has no expected value to compare against and cannot be run as specified.
objections.evidence: "Integration smoke test" step 6: "assert it appears verbatim in the named file at PIN … and that the nearest preceding heading is the one the map names." The map's quote cells (e.g. the amendment-surface quotes, the `governance-profile.js` comment quote) name `file:line`, never a heading.
objections.predicted_consequence: The builder either silently skips the heading clause for unnamed-heading quotes (the recorded smoke-test run then claims a check it did not perform) or invents heading names post hoc to make step 6 pass — either way the map's "All eight steps pass" record is not the check the procedure defines.

objections.claim: DONE requires "Every cited line range in the map is correct at the pin: an inline-selftest range starts on the line declaring the named function and ends on its closing line; a quoted line number is the line holding the quote" — newly tightened in this spec ("end lines included"). But none of the eight smoke-test steps checks line ranges: step 6 checks quotes verbatim and headings, step 7 checks module/function existence. The spec's Why section says the revision is proven "with the map's own eight-step smoke test," so a DONE item the proof mechanism does not decide is a gap the spec must close in place (either a line-range check in step 6/7 or an explicit statement that line ranges are verified by a named manual pass recorded in the smoke-test section).
objections.evidence: "From how (rows and prose)" checklist line-range item vs. smoke-test steps 1–8, none of which resolve a cited line number.
objections.predicted_consequence: A build can pass all eight recorded steps while a cited selftest range is off by lines (the exact class of drift the spec itself lists at `b02fac1b`: `buildClaimSelftest` 1637→1519, etc.), and the map's smoke-test record still reads as a full verification.
